data.name: Anjum
data.gender_notes: Anjum is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Anjum is an Arabic name meaning 'stars' or 'celestial bodies'. It symbolizes guidance, light, and divine beauty. Used for both boys and girls, it reflects brilliance and hope. The name Anjum carries the meaning “Stars, Celestial Bodies” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Anjum usually hope their child will grow to embody stars, celestial bodies and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents divine light—like stars guiding lost souls in the darkness.
data.etymology: Anjum belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Stars, Celestial Bodies.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Anjum total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_arabic.name: أنجوم
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم أنجوم مشتق من الجذر النجمي، ويشير إلى مجموعة من النجوم في السماء، ويعبر عن الجمال والتنوع في خلق الله، كما ورد في القرآن الكريم في سورة الأنعام: 'وَهُوَ الَّذِي يَبُثُ النُّجُومَ فِي السَّمَاءِ'

in_urdu.name: انجم
in_urdu.long_meaning: انجم کا نام عربی زبان کی نجم جڑ سے بنا ہے، جو ستاروں کے مجموعے کو ظاہر کرتا ہے، یہ نام جنوبی ایشیائی مسلمانوں میں مقبول ہے، اور اسلامی ثقافت میں خوبصورتی اور تنوع کی علامت ہے

in_hindi.name: अनजुम
in_hindi.long_meaning: अनजुम नाम की उत्पत्ति अरबी भाषा से हुई है, जिसका अर्थ है सितारों का समूह, यह नाम भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में बहुत लोकप्रिय है, और यह इस्लामी संस्कृति में सौंदर्य और विविधता का प्रतीक है

in_pashto.name: انجوم
in_pashto.long_meaning: انجوم نوم د عربی ژبې د نجم ريښې څخه اخیستل شوی دی، کوم چې د ستورو ګروپ څرګندوي، دا نوم د افغان او پښتون قومونو لپاره د ښکلا او تنوع سمبول دی

in_english.name: Anjum
in_english.long_meaning: Anjum originates from the Arabic root 'najm', signifying a group of stars or celestial bodies, mentioned in the Quran in Surah An-Najm, symbolizing beauty, guidance, and divine creation in Islamic tradition

data.cultural_impact: The name Anjum may not have any specific cultural significance in and of itself, as it is an Arabic name widely used across various Islamic communities. However, it can be linked to the rich Islamic literary and cultural traditions that celebrate the idea of stars as symbols of guidance. In Islamic poetry and literature, stars are often depicted as guiding lights, a reflection of Allah's wisdom and guidance in the universe.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Anjum lies in its symbolic representation of the divine light and guidance in the universe. Stars, being celestial bodies, are seen as a reminder of the vastness of the universe and the omnipresence of Allah. In Islamic tradition, stars are believed to have been created by Allah as a means of guidance and to serve as a reminder of His existence. The name Anjum can serve as a constant reminder to its bearer of the divine guidance and light that exists in the universe and within oneself. Additionally, the name represents the idea of hope, as stars serve as guiding lights even in the darkest of nights, and the name can inspire its bearer to persevere and find light in the face of adversity.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Anjum means "rest" or "lodging" in Arabic. In the spiritual context, it can symbolize finding inner peace and tranquility, a place of refuge in times of hardship or distress. It can also represent a place of learning and growth, where one can seek knowledge and wisdom.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Anjum is mentioned in the works of Al-Kindi as a rare name in the 9th century The name Anjum carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Anjum was used in the Arabic-speaking world during the Islamic Golden Age

trends: increasing popularity in the UK and US
modern_usage.modern_context: The name Anjum remains relevant in modern Muslim society, representing a bridge between traditional Islamic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Islamic names.
